A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BOLD study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on three video-language models across four video-MCQA benchmarks, including input perturbations, calibration results and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original model-performance, selection-bias and calibration results in Tables 2–3 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: Both versions use three missing-component priors, sample-averaged global calibration and the COBYLA-based Weighted_BOLD variant. Algorithms 1–2 match apart from equation references; expanded explanations do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both use NExT-QA/NExT-GQA, STAR, Perception Test and Video-MME with the same eleven input modifications. V2's new Table 4 illustrates existing scenarios rather than introducing additional coverage.

E2.justification: The same default, BOLD and Weighted_BOLD comparisons remain for Video-LLaMA, Video-LLaVA and SeViLA. No additional debiasing baseline is evaluated; PriDe remains related-work discussion.

E3.justification: Splits, the stratified 40% Perception Test subset, Video-MME balancing, model configurations, prompts, metrics and calibration sample fractions are retained. V2's statement that answer shuffling occurs once adds documentation rather than revising a previously stated setting.

E4.justification: The component perturbations, SeViLA shifted-option check, sample-fraction sweeps and positive-versus-negative weight analyses are retained. The new worked example and summarized plots do not add an ablation or robustness evaluation.

E5.justification: Both Appendix D sections specify random seed 1. No repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or statistical testing procedures are added. The retained standard-deviation metrics measure disparities across answer options.

E6.justification: V2's Figures 2–4 newly report an averaged 'All Each' distribution pooling the existing identical-answer variants. Tables 2–3 and all matched appendix result tables are numerically unchanged. The addition is an aggregate summary, not a performance improvement.

T1.justification: V2 removes the equal-difficulty assumption and the bias set-inclusion expression, explicitly defines binary task well-definedness and formalizes component-removal attacks. It also adds geometric reasoning about weight constraints. The calibration equations remain equivalent, and no proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims about the first video-MCQA selection-bias study and effective BOLD calibration remain. V2's conclusion additionally claims applicability to 'any existing VLM', broadening the stated applicability beyond v1's wording.

C2.justification: V2 newly acknowledges that calibration was primarily assessed on original datasets rather than systematically across all modifications. Section 3.4 also adds an explanation linking SeViLA's first-option preference under identical answers to argmax tie-breaking.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code-repository link where v1 promised future code/data release. It also specifies one shuffle and describes Video-LLaVA's linear projector. Most model settings and prompts are retained or relocated, rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: V2 adds Haladyna (2004) to support test-item requirements and Xiao et al. (2023) for NExT-GQA. Positioning relative to PriDe, multimodal debiasing and permutation methods remains substantially unchanged; duplicate references to existing works do not expand research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the introduction, dataset/model descriptions, experimental rationales, observations and conclusion. It redistributes technical descriptions into the appendices and divides Appendix C into examples and performance, substantially revising the narrative despite stable experiments.

P2.justification: The three principal distribution figures are redesigned around accuracy-irrelevant settings and aggregated summaries. Full distributions are redrawn and relocated as Figures 25–27, and Table 4 adds worked modification examples. This substantially changes presentation of the empirical evidence.

improvement.justification: Clearer main plots, worked examples, code-access information and an explicit validation limitation modestly improve readability and reproducibility guidance. These gains outweigh a localized mathematical overstatement in Section 4.2.2: bounded weights are called a convex combination without a sum-to-one constraint. The underlying method and performance evidence remain unchanged.
